title: Channel Update
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1APEiSZz2zM

After roughly three months away, Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to explain the silence and, in the process, states the operating principle the channel has run on ever since. Two reasons for the gap: the recording room becomes unbearable under lights in summer, and — the real one — his hobbies move in extreme cyclical phases. Something clicks, the season turns, and he is wholly elsewhere. This summer it was David Lynch: every film rewatched, *Twin Peaks: The Return* finally watched with his wife, every book on Lynch he could find bought. *Fire Walk With Me* is his favourite; he has long wanted to write a book about it.

The announcement is that the channel will widen to books and film. Not, he is careful to say, as a geek-culture channel — more a personal vlog about the fantasy, horror and weird fiction he loves, on the grounds that his taste in games, films and books is one taste, not three. A stack of autumn horror reading is shown off: Matthew M. Bartlett, Norman Partridge's *Dark Harvest*, Bradbury's *The October Country*, Sturgeon, King's *Cycle of the Werewolf*.

He is blunt about the cost. Some people came for board games and will leave; that is fine. He cannot force interest he doesn't have, and the channel only continues if it stays interesting to him.

----

Is a creator's honesty about cyclical interest a strength or a liability when an audience subscribed to one specific thing?
